correctness.rationale: The graph-state character sum gives a flat reduced spectrum whose logarithmic rank is the binary rank of cross-adjacency. For codimension >=2, row differences have k independent linear parts; a constant occurs exactly for nonisotropic U, while the nondegenerate quadratic weight 2^(d-1) +/- 2^(d/2-1) excludes the base row from the affine span. Hyperplanes have restricted polar rank d-2 and a non-affine quadratic base row, giving rank d. This proves all boundaries and affine offsets; exactly 8952 finite binary ranks and eight direct quantum spectra independently corroborate the formula without being substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural highly symmetric strongly regular graph family, with exponentially many quantum sites, has its complete affine-linear-code cut entanglement spectrum evaluated by symplectic isotropy and dimension. The one-ebit isotropy transition and complete insensitivity to the Arf refinement are structural phenomena; even different-degree nonisomorphic quantum-network graphs share the same entire affine-flat entanglement profile. This is a nontrivial all-parameter invariant classification, not a parameter substitution or numerical table.
